description: A false-colour infrared satellite map, derived from Spot 5 imagery (2.5 m resolution, 1/2/3 band combination) dated 2011-07-23, illustrates the application of generalization rules for delineating low urban density areas within the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS). The map shows a rural/peri-urban landscape where vegetation appears in various shades of red, and urban structures/bare soil appear in light blue or grey. A continuous yellow polygonal outline defines a "low urban density area" (labeled "1110") stretching across the image. The delineation demonstrates specific mapping rules regarding gap closure: sections marked "< 50 m" indicate that narrow gaps between urban features, less than 50 metres in width, are included within the continuous urban boundary. Conversely, a section marked "> 50 m" shows a wider gap that causes the urban delineation to be split into separate polygons, as it exceeds the maximum width for gap closure. This visually explains how spatial rules are applied to maintain the continuity of urban fabric, preventing underestimation of low urban density areas by including private gardens and closing gaps up to 50 m.
